pages.subtitle: The very old church in Bethlehem built over the place where Christians remember Jesus was born.

quick_facts.label: First church built
quick_facts.value: 300s, in the time of Emperor Constantine

quick_facts.label: Cared for by
quick_facts.value: Catholic Franciscans, Greek Orthodox and Armenian Christians

pages.intro: In the town of Bethlehem stands one of the oldest churches in the world, the Basilica of the Nativity. "Nativity" means birth. Under the church is a cave called the Grotto of the Nativity. For many centuries, Christians have honored this cave as the place where Mary gave birth to Jesus and laid him in a manger.
story_paragraphs: The Gospel of Luke tells us that the Roman emperor ordered everyone to be counted. So Joseph traveled from Nazareth to Bethlehem, the town of King David, with Mary, who was expecting a baby.

While they were in Bethlehem, Mary gave birth to her son, Jesus. She wrapped him in cloths and laid him in a manger, because there was no room for them in the inn. That night, angels told shepherds in the fields the good news, and the shepherds hurried to see the baby. The Gospel of Matthew tells us that wise men from the East later followed a star to Bethlehem to honor him.

Long after, a Roman emperor named Hadrian built a pagan shrine over the cave. But Christians remembered the place. In the 300s, Emperor Constantine and his mother, Saint Helena, had a great church built over the cave.
In the 500s, the church was damaged. Emperor Justinian rebuilt it even bigger. Much of the church he built still stands today, making it one of the oldest churches still in use anywhere in the world.

To enter, people go through a very small doorway called the Door of Humility. It was made low long ago to keep people from riding in on horses. Today, almost everyone has to bow down to go through it.

Below the church, in the grotto, a silver star with fourteen points marks the place where Christians remember Jesus was born. Nearby, Saint Jerome lived in a cave in the 300s while he translated the Bible into Latin.

Today, Catholic Franciscans, Greek Orthodox and Armenian Christians share the care of the church. Christians from around the world come here to pray and to remember that God came to us as a little child.

pages.subtitle: The church in Nazareth where Christians remember the angel Gabriel's message to Mary.

quick_facts.label: Bible event
quick_facts.value: The angel Gabriel's message to Mary

pages.intro: In the town of Nazareth stands a large church called the Basilica of the Annunciation. "Annunciation" means an announcement. Here, Christians remember the day the angel Gabriel came to Mary and told her she would be the mother of Jesus, the Son of God. Inside the church is a small cave, and on its altar are the words, "Here the Word was made flesh."
story_paragraphs: Mary was a young Jewish woman who lived in Nazareth, a small village in Galilee. She was engaged to marry a carpenter named Joseph.

One day, God sent the angel Gabriel to Mary. The angel said, "Hail, favored one! The Lord is with you." Mary was confused and wondered what the greeting meant. The angel told her not to be afraid. She would have a son, and she would name him Jesus. He would be called the Son of the Most High.

Mary asked how this could happen. The angel explained that the Holy Spirit would come upon her, and that nothing is impossible for God. Then Mary said, "Behold, I am the handmaid of the Lord. May it be done to me according to your word." Mary said yes to God.

Christians have honored a small cave in Nazareth as part of Mary's home. Below the church today are the remains of a building used for worship in the 300s. A pilgrim wrote about a church here in about the year 570. Later, Crusaders built a huge cathedral, but it was destroyed in the 1200s.
For a long time, only ruins were left. In 1620, Franciscan friars came to stay in Nazareth for good, and they have cared for the holy place ever since.

The church that stands today was finished in 1969. It is built in two levels. The lower church surrounds the cave. The upper church is decorated with pictures of Mary sent by Catholics from many countries, showing Mary in the clothing and styles of their own people.
When Catholics pray the Hail Mary or the Angelus, they repeat the angel's greeting and remember Mary's yes.

pages.subtitle: The church in Galilee where Christians remember Jesus' first miracle, at a wedding feast.

quick_facts.label: Bible event
quick_facts.value: Jesus turns water into wine at a wedding

pages.intro: In a town in Galilee called Kafr Kanna stands the Wedding Church of Cana. Here, Christians remember Jesus' very first miracle. At a wedding feast, the wine ran out, and Mary asked Jesus to help. Jesus turned water into wine. Every year, many married couples come to this church to pray and to renew the promises they made on their wedding day.
story_paragraphs: The Gospel of John tells us that there was a wedding in the village of Cana in Galilee. Mary, the mother of Jesus, was there. Jesus and his disciples were invited too.
In those days, a wedding feast could last for days. But during this feast, the wine ran out. That would have been very embarrassing for the bride and groom.
Mary noticed. She went to Jesus and said, "They have no wine." Then she said to the servants, "Do whatever he tells you."

Nearby stood six large stone water jars. Jesus told the servants to fill them with water, and they filled them to the brim. Then he told them to draw some out and take it to the headwaiter. When the headwaiter tasted it, the water had become wine. He was amazed. He told the groom that he had saved the best wine for last.
Saint John says this was the first of Jesus' signs. It showed his glory, and his disciples began to believe in him.

Christians in the Byzantine period wrote that the wedding took place in Kafr Kanna. In 1641, Franciscan friars acquired land there, and the church that stands today was finished in 1879. Under the church, people can see the remains of an old house, which tradition says is where the wedding took place.

Today, three Franciscan friars care for the church and the parish. On the feast that remembers the wedding, many couples from the parish renew their wedding promises. Mary's words still ring out at Cana: "Do whatever he tells you."

pages.student_title: The Church of the Transfiguration on Mount Tabor
pages.subtitle: The church on a mountain in Galilee where Christians remember Jesus shining with God's glory.
pages.intro: Mount Tabor is a round mountain that rises above the plains of Galilee. On top of it stands the Church of the Transfiguration. Here, Christians remember the day Jesus took three of his apostles up a high mountain. His face shone like the sun, and his clothes became white as light. A voice from heaven said, "This is my beloved Son."
story_paragraphs: One day, Jesus took three of his apostles, Peter, James and John, and led them up a high mountain to pray.

While Jesus was praying, he was transfigured, which means his appearance was changed. His face shone like the sun, and his clothes became dazzling white. Then two great men from long ago appeared and talked with Jesus. They were Moses, who gave God's Law to the people, and Elijah, the great prophet.

Peter was so amazed that he did not know what to say. He offered to build three tents, one for Jesus, one for Moses and one for Elijah. While he was still speaking, a bright cloud covered them. A voice came from the cloud: "This is my beloved Son, with whom I am well pleased; listen to him."
The apostles fell to the ground in fear. But Jesus came and touched them and said, "Rise, and do not be afraid." When they looked up, they saw only Jesus.

The Gospels do not name the mountain. Since early times, Christians have remembered Mount Tabor as the place. People have prayed here since the Byzantine era, and Crusaders and Benedictine monks later built churches and a monastery on the mountain.

In the 1870s, Franciscan friars built a monastery on Tabor. Then, from 1921 to 1924, they built the beautiful basilica that stands there today. It was designed by an Italian architect named Antonio Barluzzi. Its two towers stand over old chapels honoring Moses and Elijah.
The Transfiguration gave the apostles a glimpse of who Jesus truly is: the Son of God. It helped prepare them for the hard days ahead, when Jesus would suffer and die before rising again.

pages.subtitle: The room in Jerusalem where Christians remember the Last Supper and the coming of the Holy Spirit.

quick_facts.label: Bible event
quick_facts.value: The Last Supper and, by tradition, Pentecost

quick_facts.label: First church built
quick_facts.value: Today's room comes from a Crusader chapel of the 1100s

quick_facts.label: Cared for by
quick_facts.value: The government of Israel; Franciscans pray there on special days

pages.intro: On Mount Zion in Jerusalem is a stone room called the Cenacle, or the Upper Room. Here, Christians remember the Last Supper, when Jesus gave us the Eucharist and washed his apostles' feet. By tradition, it is also where the Holy Spirit came down on the apostles at Pentecost. Some call it the place where the Church was born.
story_paragraphs: On the night before he died, Jesus wanted to celebrate the Passover meal with his apostles. He sent two of them into Jerusalem, where a man showed them a large upper room, ready for the meal.

During the supper, Jesus did something surprising. He got up, tied a towel around his waist, and washed his apostles' feet, the job of a servant. He told them, "I have given you a model to follow, so that as I have done for you, you should also do."

Then Jesus took bread, blessed it, broke it, and gave it to them, saying, "This is my body." He took a cup of wine and said, "This is my blood." This was the first Eucharist. At every Mass, Catholics remember and celebrate what Jesus did that night.

After Jesus rose from the dead and went up to heaven, the apostles gathered in the upper room with Mary to pray. On the feast of Pentecost, a sound like a strong wind filled the house, and tongues like fire rested on each of them. They were filled with the Holy Spirit and began to tell everyone about Jesus.

The room on Mount Zion that stands today is not the same room from Jesus' time. It was restored from a chapel the Crusaders built in the 1100s. In the 1300s, the Franciscan friars received the site, and it became their first home in the Holy Land.
In 1551, the Franciscans were forced to leave. Over the centuries, the room was used as a mosque. Below it is a shrine that Jewish tradition honors as the tomb of King David.
Today, the government of Israel cares for the building. The Franciscans may gather there to pray on Holy Thursday and Pentecost, remembering what happened in the upper room.

pages.student_title: The Church of All Nations in Gethsemane
pages.subtitle: The church in an olive garden in Jerusalem where Christians remember Jesus praying the night before he died.

quick_facts.label: Bible event
quick_facts.value: Jesus prays in the Garden of Gethsemane

quick_facts.label: First church built
quick_facts.value: 300s, in the time of Emperor Theodosius

pages.intro: At the foot of the Mount of Olives in Jerusalem is a garden of very old olive trees called Gethsemane. Next to it stands the Church of All Nations. Christians remember that Jesus came here to pray on the night before he died. Inside the church is a large rock where, by tradition, Jesus knelt and prayed to his Father.
story_paragraphs: After the Last Supper, Jesus and his apostles sang a hymn and walked out of the city. They crossed a valley and came to a garden on the Mount of Olives called Gethsemane.
Jesus asked his apostles to wait and pray. He took Peter, James and John a little farther with him. He told them his heart was full of sorrow, and he asked them to stay awake with him.

Then Jesus went a short distance away and fell to the ground to pray. He knew that he was about to suffer. He prayed, "My Father, if it is possible, let this cup pass from me; yet, not as I will, but as you will." Jesus trusted his Father completely.
When Jesus came back, he found the apostles asleep. They were tired and sad. He asked them again to stay awake and pray. Three times he went off to pray, and three times he found them sleeping.
Then Judas, one of the twelve, came into the garden with a crowd, and Jesus was arrested. Even then, Jesus was calm and peaceful, because he had given himself completely to his Father's will.

In the 300s, a church was built over the rock where Christians remembered Jesus praying. Later, the Crusaders built another church there. The church that stands today was finished in 1924. It was designed by Antonio Barluzzi, and Catholics from many countries helped pay for it. That is why it is called the Church of All Nations.

Inside, purple and blue windows let in only a little light, so the church feels like a garden at night. Around the rock is a metal crown of thorns. Outside, Franciscan friars care for the olive trees, some of them hundreds of years old.

type_specific.now: A large church with a bright mosaic on its front stands beside the garden, and some of the olive trees are hundreds of years old.
type_specific.what_historians_know: a church was built over the rock in the 300s, and a pilgrim named Egeria described an "elegant church" here. Scientists studied the oldest olive trees in 2012 and found that their trunks go back about 900 years.
type_specific.what_comes_from_tradition: that this is the exact garden and the exact rock where Jesus prayed. The Gospels say he went to the Mount of Olives, but no one can prove the exact spot.

quiz.prompt: What does "Gethsemane" mean?
quiz.explanation: "Gethsemane" means "oil press," a place where olives were crushed to make oil.

quiz.prompt: What did Jesus do in the garden?
quiz.explanation: Jesus went to the garden to pray the night before he died.

quiz.prompt: What were the apostles doing when Jesus came back?
quiz.explanation: Three times Jesus came back and found the apostles asleep.

quiz.prompt: Why is it called the Church of All Nations?

choices.text: Catholics from many countries helped pay for it

quiz.explanation: Catholics from many countries helped pay for the church, and their coats of arms decorate the ceiling.

quiz.prompt: What did Jesus pray?

choices.text: "Not as I will, but as you will."

quiz.explanation: Jesus trusted his Father completely and prayed that his Father's will be done.
